clean_room_boundary.statement: The lane derives the finite-max bundle formula from the published objective and generic gradient-sampling mathematics. No repository source, paper coefficient table, Arena candidate value, retained NumPy payload, or SimpleTES value is used.

sources.title: Further Improvements to the Lower Bound for an Autoconvolution Inequality
used_claims: The direct objective uses Simpson-style L2 integration, a Riemann-sum L1 term, and the largest convolution entry.
Fresh random populations, high-learning-rate noisy exploration, lower-learning-rate exploitation, and elitist respawn were effective at modest resolution.
The reported extremizer has a tall asymmetric spike plus a right-hand comb, and the authors explicitly propose tailored comb initializers.
Peak flattening distinguishes this objective, while navigating its nonsmooth surface remains open.

sources.title: Gradient Sampling Methods for Nonsmooth Optimization
used_claims: Near a nonsmooth point, gradients from nearby differentiable points can stabilize a search direction.
The robust direction uses the minimum-norm element of the convex hull of sampled gradients.
The convex-hull calculation is a small strongly convex simplex QP equivalent to a bundle subproblem.
sources.scope_limit: The C2 objective is maximized and has nonnegativity/simplex geometry, so the lane uses the finite-branch maximin dual as a heuristic specialization; no convergence theorem is claimed.

sources.title: An improved example for an autoconvolution inequality
sources.used_claim: The exact finite-step formula and the 23-to-115-to-575 optimization hierarchy independently support the formula audit and resolution-specific search premise.

sources.title: ImprovEvolve: Basin-Hopping Meets LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
sources.used_claim: Separating initialization, local improvement, and intensity-scheduled perturbation operators improved the reported C2 lower bound; this supports an explicit population lifecycle rather than a monolithic local solve.
